test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: To get a virtual, erect and enlarged image using a spherical mirror, the object must be placed _____________.

options.text: at the principal focus (F) of a convex mirror
at the principal focus (F) of a concave mirror
at the centre of curvature (C) of a concave mirror
between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F) of a concave mirror

solution:
The correct answer is __**between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F) of a concave mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a spherical mirror with an **inwardly curved reflecting surface**. It has the unique ability to produce both **real and virtual images** depending on the position of the object.
 
• When an object is placed **between the pole (P) and the principal focus (F)** of a **concave mirror**, the reflected rays diverge. When produced backwards, they appear to meet behind the mirror, forming a **virtual, erect, and enlarged image**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• In the case of a **convex mirror**, the image formed is **always virtual, erect, and diminished**, no matter where the object is placed. It cannot produce an enlarged virtual image. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• If an object is placed at the **principal focus (F)** of a **concave mirror**, the reflected rays emerge parallel to each other. This results in an image formed at **infinity**, which is **real, inverted, and highly enlarged**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• When the object is positioned at the **centre of curvature (C)** of a **concave mirror**, the image is formed exactly at **C**. This image is **real, inverted, and the same size** as the object. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **nature of the image** (real or virtual) is determined by whether the light rays actually intersect or only appear to intersect after reflection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror (Converging Mirror):**
 
 
• These mirrors **converge** light rays falling on them. They are used in **torches, searchlights, and vehicle headlights** to get powerful parallel beams of light.
 
• In the field of medicine, **dentists** use concave mirrors to see **enlarged images** of the teeth of patients.
 
• Large concave mirrors are also utilized to concentrate **solar energy** in solar furnaces.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror (Diverging Mirror):**
 
 
• These mirrors **diverge** light rays. They are commonly used as **rear-view (wing) mirrors** in vehicles.
 
• They are preferred because they always give an **erect, though diminished, image** and have a **wider field of view** as they are curved outwards.
 
 
 
• **Important Optical Terms:**
 
 
• **Pole (P):** The center of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror.
 
• **Principal Focus (F):** The point on the principal axis where parallel rays of light **converge** (concave) or appear to **diverge** from (convex) after reflection.
 
• **Focal Length (f):** The distance between the **Pole** and the **Principal Focus**. The radius of curvature (R) is twice the focal length (**R = 2f**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirror Formula:** The relationship between the object distance (**u**), image distance (**v**), and focal length (**f**) is expressed as **1/v + 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• **Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object (**m = h'/h**). It is also related to distances as **m = -v/u**.
 
• For a **virtual and erect image**, the magnification (**m**) is always **positive**. In the case of the object between P and F of a concave mirror, **m > 1** because the image is enlarged.
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the focal length of a **concave mirror** is **negative**, while that of a **convex mirror** is **positive**.
